ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB \parallel EF$, $\angle ABC = 75^\circ$, $\angle CDF = 135^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle BCD$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let point $G$ be the intersection of $BC$ and $EF$, as shown in the diagram below: \\
$\because$ $AB\parallel EF$, $\angle ABC=75^\circ$, $\angle CDF=135^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle EGC=\angle ABC=75^\circ$, $\angle EDC=180^\circ-\angle CDF=180^\circ-135^\circ=45^\circ$,\\
Furthermore, $\because$ $\angle EGC=\angle BCD+\angle EDC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle BCD=75^\circ-45^\circ=\boxed{30^\circ}$.

raw_record.question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB \parallel EF$, $\angle ABC = 75^\circ$, $\angle CDF = 135^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle BCD$ in degrees?

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as two horizontal parallel lines, with AB on the top line and EF on the lower line; BC is a slanted transversal through B down to C, and CD is another slanted segment from C to D on EF. From the text, use AB ∥ EF, ∠ABC = 75°, and ∠CDF = 135°. Since AB is parallel to EF, the angle that CB makes with the lower parallel is 75° by corresponding/alternate angle reasoning. At D, ∠CDF = 135° is measured with the rightward ray DF, so the acute angle that CD makes with the lower parallel on the other side is 180° − 135° = 45°. The desired angle ∠BCD is the difference between the directions of CB and CD relative to the same parallel line: 75° − 45° = 30°.

method.method_draft: Use the visible intersection point G where line BC crosses EF, forming triangle CGD. From the image, G and D both lie on the lower horizontal line EF, C is below it, and the desired angle ∠BCD is the same as triangle angle ∠GCD because B, G, and C are collinear. From ∠CDF = 135°, the interior angle at D of triangle CGD is ∠CDG = 180° − 135° = 45°, since DG and DF are opposite rays on EF. From AB ∥ EF and ∠ABC = 75°, transfer the 75° angle to the corresponding angle at G between GE and GC; therefore the interior angle at G between GC and GD is its supplement, 180° − 75° = 105°. Then use the triangle angle sum in triangle CGD: ∠GCD = 180° − 45° − 105° = 30°. Hence ∠BCD = 30°.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中上方有一条水平线段 AB，下方有一条与其平行的水平线 EF。斜线 BC 从 B 向下经过 EF 上的交点 G，继续到 C；点 D 也在 EF 上，且 C 与 D 相连。图中标出 ∠ABC = 75°，∠CDF = 135°。要求的是 C 点处由 CB 与 CD 形成的 ∠BCD。

推理：设 BC 与 EF 的交点为 G，则 B、G、C 共线，所以 ∠BCD 与三角形 CGD 中的 ∠GCD 相同。因为 D、G、F 在同一直线 EF 上，DG 与 DF 是相反方向的射线，而 ∠CDF = 135°，所以三角形 CGD 在 D 点的内角 ∠CDG = 180° - 135° = 45°。又因为 AB ∥ EF，且 ∠ABC = 75°，对应到 G 点可得 GE 与 GC 所成的角为 75°。三角形 CGD 在 G 点的内角是 GC 与 GD 所成的角，它与 75° 互补，所以 ∠CGD = 180° - 75° = 105°。因此在三角形 CGD 中，∠GCD = 180° - 45° - 105° = 30°。所以 ∠BCD = 30°。
